failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector never fires on ANY scenario (0 detections, 0 false positives everywhere). The root cause is a SIGN INVERSION in the directional (split-ratio) shape test. For this plant the controlled tank's loop is paired with the pump that feeds it (h1<->v1, h2<->v2). A leak in tank1 makes h1 sag, so v1 (the tank1 pump) is driven up; since v1 up also over-feeds h2, v2 is driven down. Net effect: the pump split (v1-v2) moves in the SAME direction as the tank index, i.e. dS>0 for a tank1 leak and dS<0 for a tank2 leak. The champion coded the opposite (tank1_full requires dS<=-1.3*dT and tank2_full requires dS>=+1.3*dT), so the full+recent conjunction is logically unsatisfiable and the whole detector is unreachable dead code. The secondary bug is the err_ok gate: it demands block-mean |error|<0.16, but healthy |error| is already 0.074/0.083 (so it gives zero baseline protection) while a real leak RAISES error, so the gate can only suppress genuine detections. Symmetric 'both-pump' faults (both_leaks) also had no reachable path at all.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Flip the split-shape sign so tank1 uses dS>0 and tank2 uses dS<0, drop the error cap from the directional path, keep the tight ratio band as the baseline discriminator (healthy anti-phase oscillation produces large |dS| with near-zero dT, which the ratio band rejects), add a conservative symmetric 'both pumps overloaded, split near anchor, both errors elevated' fallback for both_leaks, and keep the full-window + recent-half conjunction so only sustained faults are ever flagged.

self_check: Measured healthy anchors: mean(v1+v2)=10.42+7.33=17.75 ~ TOT_ANCHOR=17.77; mean(v1-v2)=3.05=SPLIT_ANCHOR. Directional gate for EITHER tank needs dT>2.8, i.e. a 50-sample block-mean total effort > 20.57 V. On baseline the block-mean total stays within roughly +/-1.5 V of 17.75 (the pumps oscillate ANTI-phase: when v1 is high v2 is low, so the SUM barely moves), giving typical dT ~ -0.02 to +1.5, far below 2.8 -> no fire. Even the worst measured excursion pair (v1=12,v2=12, total=24, dT=6.23) does NOT flag: with both rails at 12, split=0 so dS=-3.05, but the tank1 band demands dS in [1.30*6.23, 2.60*6.23]=[8.1,16.2] (fails) and the tank2 band demands dS in [-16.2,-8.1] (fails). A one-sided healthy extreme (v1=12,v2=2.54) gives total 14.54 -> dT<0 -> fails the dT gate. More importantly, during healthy oscillation the large split excursions occur while dT is near zero, so |dS|/dT is huge and never lands inside [1.30,2.60] -> the ratio band rejects pure control-interaction swings. Recent-half gate needs dTr>2.2 with ratio>1.05, same reasoning. Errors: measured block-mean |e1|=0.074, |e2|=0.083; the symmetric fallback requires BOTH block-means > 0.14 simultaneously (measured peaks are 0.19 but are transient, so a 50-sample mean reaching 0.14 on BOTH tanks at once essentially never happens), plus dT>3.2 and |dS|<0.6*dT -> baseline-safe. Therefore, for tank1 typical dT~(-0.02..1.5) vs gate 2.8 (fail, margin ~1.3-2.8 V) and for tank2 typical dS swings vs its required ratio band (fail); neither tank trips.
proposed_change: 1) Reverse the shape sign: tank1 anomaly now requires dS>+LO*dT (v1 over-pumping), tank2 requires dS<-LO*dT (v2 over-pumping). 2) Delete the err_ok cap from the directional path (it cannot protect baseline and only blocks faults that raise error). 3) Keep the full-window AND recent-half conjunction (sustained-only) and the tight ratio band [1.30,2.60]/[1.05,3.20] as the FP discriminator against anti-phase oscillation. 4) Add a conservative symmetric fallback: if dT>3.2 (dTr>2.4) AND |dS|<0.60*dT AND both block-mean |errors|>0.14 (sustained), flag BOTH tanks (catches both_leaks where the split stays near its anchor). 5) Keep the setpoint adaptation/restoration logic unchanged.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The directional detector is gated on a RISE in total pump effort (DT_GATE=2.8 V full / 2.2 V recent on mean(v1+v2)). This is physically unreachable here: v1's healthy mean is already 10.42 V with only ~1.6 V of headroom to its 12 V rail, so even a full tank1 leak pins v1 at ~12 V and can raise the two-pump total by at most ~1.6 V (less if v2 de-loads), never 2.8 V. The recent-half gate (2.2 V) is also unreachable, so tank1 leaks are missed on every step (250 missed). The ratio band dS in [1.30,2.60]*dT is likewise unsatisfiable when only one pump saturates, because then dS/dT = +/-1 exactly, outside the band, and if the anti-phase cross-coupled tank de-loads, dT collapses toward zero and the band shrinks to nothing. Result: massive misses on every fault (1102 total) and post-clear false flags (the 50-sample full-window test keeps firing ~50 steps after a fault ends). The unused headroom is in the tanks' own tracking error, which rises sustainably on the faulted loop while the healthy, directly-actuated loop re-regulates.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Abandon the total-effort-rise gate (unreachable given pump-rail saturation) and switch the primary detector to each tank's OWN sustained block-mean |error| (recent ~20-sample window plus full 50-sample window), which sits far outside the measured healthy envelope (mean|e1|=0.0743, mean|e2|=0.0832, max instantaneous 0.19). Use the tank's own pump effort deviation from its measured healthy mean (either rail) only as a loose secondary confirmation, and use a short recent window to clear flags quickly after a fault ends so post-clear false positives drop.

self_check: Window facts: n is always 50; I use R=20 (<=50) and the full 50-sample block, no gate requires >50 samples. TANK1 baseline: healthy mean|e1|=0.0743, max instantaneous |e1|=0.19. My recent-20 gate is e1r>0.13 and full-50 gate e1f>0.10. A 20-sample MEAN of 0.13 would require ~70% of samples pinned at the 0.19 peak, which is impossible when the episode average is 0.0743; the observed 20-block mean sits near 0.074 (about 0.53x the gate). The 50-block mean is likewise ~0.074 < 0.10. So tank1_err is False on baseline. Effort confirmation |v1r-10.42|>0.80 needs v1r>11.22 (or <9.62) AND tank1_err True; on baseline high-v1 blocks coincide with the level rising (small/negative error), so the joint condition never holds. Net: tank1 flag False on baseline. TANK2 baseline: healthy mean|e2|=0.0832, max |e2|=0.1905; recent-20 gate 0.14 and full-50 gate 0.11 both exceed the healthy block mean (0.083) by >1.3x, so e2r>0.14 / e2f>0.11 never happen on baseline (a 20-mean of 0.14 would need most samples above the 0.19 peak). Effort gate |v2r-7.33|>1.00 needs v2r>8.33 (or <6.33) jointly with e2r>0.14, which does not co-occur on the fault-free episode. Net: tank2 flag False. Both instantaneous maxima (0.19, 0.1905) are handled because I gate on BLOCK MEANS and separately require E_STRONG=0.21 (above the largest measured instantaneous |error|) before overriding the effort check.
proposed_change: Replace the total-effort-rise + split-ratio detector with a per-tank, error-centred detector: (1) compute block-mean |error| and pump effort over the full 50-sample window and over the most recent 20 samples; (2) flag tank k when its OWN recent-20 mean|error| exceeds ~1.8x its measured healthy mean (tank1 0.13, tank2 0.14) AND its full-50 mean|error| exceeds ~1.3x healthy (tank1 0.10, tank2 0.11), confirmed by the tank's own pump effort having left its measured healthy band by a small margin (|v1r-10.42|>0.8, |v2r-7.33|>1.0) or by an unambiguously large recent error (>0.21); (3) keep a bounded setpoint derating on detection (LOWER_STEP=0.015, floor ~0.5*nominal) and restore toward nominal (RESTORE_STEP=0.03) whenever a tank is not anomalous. Detection uses only a 20-sample recent window plus the real 50-sample window (nothing larger), so it is reachable and clears quickly after faults end.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The champion's detector is structurally unreachable on the very fault it is meant to catch. Its directional branches are AND-gated on `dT > 2.8 V` (mean(v1+v2) minus the 17.77 V healthy anchor). In this plant both pumps already sit near their 12 V rail when healthy (v1 mean 10.42 V -> under 1.6 V of headroom) and the healthy pump backs off while the faulted one rises, so the SUM of efforts never gains 2.8 V even under a real leak. Because the code further ANDs (a) the full 50-sample block, (b) the recent block, (c) a split-band ratio tied to that same unreachable dT, the conjunction is unsatisfiable: 250/250 missed anomalies on tank1_leak, tank2_leak and both_leaks, and 199/151 missed on the two severe scenarios. The only thing that ever fires is the `both_full and both_rec` symmetric fallback (dT>3.2 with an |error|>0.14 cap), which is what produced the 50-52 false positives in tank2_leak and both_leaks (a violation of the explicit lesson that block-mean |error| caps are pure downside). Finally, because nothing is ever detected, the setpoint is never backed off, so tank1_severe_persistent accumulates 171 safety violations (85,500 of its 145,341 points) on top of its 199 misses.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Delete every effort-total / split-ratio gate (provably unreachable here) and the symmetric |error|-cap fallback (a pure false-positive source). Detect per tank with the one signal that has a tight, measured fault-free bound: the tank's own tracking error. Place the bar strictly OUTSIDE the measured healthy envelope (1.05-1.08 x the healthy maximum |error|, not any multiple of the healthy mean, which lies inside the envelope), require the departure to be sustained over the 20 most recent samples (short block -> small post-clear release lag), and keep any setpoint mitigation small and bounded so it cannot shrink the error below the detector's own margin.

self_check: Tank1 (healthy: mean|e|=0.0743, envelope [-0.0300, 0.1899]): sustained-bar = HI_MARGIN*E1_MAX = 1.08*0.1899 = 0.20509 V. The mean of any block of healthy samples is <= their maximum, which is 0.1899 < 0.20509, so even if |e1| sat pinned at its all-time healthy extreme 0.1899 for the entire 20-sample recent block, mean_e1 = 0.1899 < 0.20509 -> sustained1 False. Per-sample bar = EXT_MARGIN*E1_MAX = 1.05*0.1899 = 0.19940 > 0.1899, so no healthy sample can ever increment cnt1 -> cnt1 = 0, frac1 = 0.00 < FRAC_EXT 0.75 -> persistent1 False. Effort is NOT used in the decision, so v1 at its healthy range endpoints (1.92 V or the 12.00 V rail) cannot produce a flag. => tank1 flag never true on baseline_no_fault. Tank2 (healthy: mean|e|=0.0832, envelope [-0.0866, 0.1905]): sustained-bar = 1.08*0.1905 = 0.20574 > 0.1905 -> a 20-sample mean is <= 0.1905 < 0.20574 -> False; per-sample bar = 1.05*0.1905 = 0.20003 > 0.1905 -> cnt2 = 0, frac2 = 0.00 < 0.75 -> False. v2 saturating anywhere in [2.54, 12.00] V is irrelevant. => tank2 flag never true on baseline. Since active_setpoints == nominal_targets on the fault-free scenario, the pass-through branch leaves sp1, sp2 untouched, so the baseline IAE is bit-identical to the champion's 94.908 with 0 false positives, 0 violations, 0 restore gap.
proposed_change: Replace the unreachable effort-total/split-ratio directional detector and the |error|-cap symmetric fallback with a single per-tank sustained-error-envelope test. For each tank k the supervisor averages |error| over the 20 most recent samples and counts how many of those 20 exceed 1.05 x that tank's measured healthy maximum |error|. A tank is flagged if its recent mean exceeds 1.08 x its healthy maximum, OR if >=75% of the recent samples exceed the 1.05 x maximum per-sample bar. Both bars sit strictly outside the entire measured fault-free envelope, so healthy oscillation (including the +/-0.19 swings and rail saturation) can never cross them, while a real leak that drives the level below the setpoint pushes the error past the healthy maximum and is caught. The short (20-sample) recent block keeps the post-clear release lag at ~20 s instead of a full window. Mitigation is deliberately small and bounded: while flagged the tank's setpoint is lowered 0.005 V/step but never below 85% of nominal, and once clear it is restored 0.020/step back to nominal, keeping the mitigation amplitude inside the detector margin (no mitigate-release-reflag chatter) and driving the restore gap to zero.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The champion's bars are already baseline-safe (both sit above the measured healthy MAX |error|, so baseline_no_fault scores 0 flags / 94.9 = pure IAE). The remaining cost is not a miscalibrated bar, it is WINDOW-INDUCED LATENCY: the detector uses a 20-sample recent block for the sustained test and a 1.08x margin for the block mean (0.2051, essentially equal to the healthy maximum), so a real fault needs ~20+ samples of elevated error before the block mean/frac crosses the bar (onset latency -> missed anomalies), and needs the error to fall back and the 20-sample block to flush before releasing (offset latency -> post-clear false positives). The equal missed=51 / false_positive=51 counts on the same tank in tank1_leak, tank2_leak and the two severe scenarios are the signature of this symmetric latency, not of a wrong threshold. Compounding it, the mitigation (0.005 V/step, capped at 15% below nominal = up to 0.045 setpoint reduction) shrinks the very |error| signal that is the only evidence, so during a marginal fault the flag can release and re-fire (mitigate -> release -> re-flag chatter), adding both missed anomalies and false positives. tank1_severe_persistent additionally racks up 171 safety violations (85500 pts) because a severe persistent fault drives tank1 out of its safe level band while v1 is already at the 12 V rail; the tiny setpoint move cannot arrest that, and it is by far the single largest term in the total score.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the 'bar strictly above the measured healthy MAX' property (it is what guarantees baseline_zero FP), but (a) replace the single 20-sample decision block with a short fast block (8 samples) plus a sustained block (24 samples), both with the bar at 1.05x the healthy max, which cuts onset and offset latency roughly in half; (b) bound the total mitigation (per-step and total deviation) to well inside the 0.0095 margin between healthy max and the bar so the diagnostic error is never suppressed and no mitigate/release chatter occurs; (c) restore quickly so restore_gap stays 0. Accept the tank1_severe safety violations as fault-inherent rather than trying to fix them by driving the setpoint around, which only adds chatter and restore error.

self_check: tank1: healthy |error| mean 0.0743, measured MAX 0.1899. Decision bar bar1 = 1.05 * 0.1899 = 0.19945. Fast test = mean of last <=8 samples of |error|; a mean is always <= the maximum of its samples, so even in the pathological healthy case where all 8 samples sit at the healthy maximum the fast mean is 0.1899 < 0.19945 -> False. Sustained test = mean of last <=24 samples <= 0.1899 < 0.19945 -> False. Fraction test = fraction of last 24 samples with |error| > 0.19945; since no healthy sample can exceed the measured max 0.1899, this fraction is exactly 0.0 < 0.60 -> False. So all three sub-conditions are False over the whole measured [ -0.0300, 0.1899 ] envelope, giving flag=False for tank1 on baseline_no_fault with a 0.0095 (5%) absolute safety buffer. tank2: healthy |error| mean 0.0832, measured MAX 0.1905; bar2 = 1.05 * 0.1905 = 0.20003; identical argument: healthy samples never exceed 0.1905, so fast mean <= 0.1905 < 0.20003, sustained mean <= 0.1905 < 0.20003, and fraction > 0.20003 is 0.0 < 0.60 -> flag=False, buffer 0.0095. Pump effort is used ONLY in the diagnosis string, never in the decision, so the healthy pumps hitting the 12 V rail (v1 range [1.92,12.00], v2 range [2.54,12.00]) cannot trigger a flag. The mitigation cap is nominal*0.98 = 0.294 (tank1) / 0.343 (tank2), i.e. at most a 0.006/0.007 setpoint deviation, far inside the 0.0095 detection margin, so the mitigation can never push the fault's own evidence below the bar.
proposed_change: Replace the single 20-sample decision window with a two-timescale detector on the same baseline-safe statistic |error|: (1) a fast block of the 8 most recent samples whose mean must exceed 1.05x the healthy MAX (0.19945 / 0.20003), which cuts onset latency and gives a prompt release once a fault clears; (2) a sustained block of the 24 most recent samples with the same bar; (3) a persistence fraction (>=60% of the 24-sample block above the bar). The block-mean bar is dropped from 1.08x to 1.05x the healthy MAX (still strictly above it, so baseline FP stays identically zero by construction), which makes the sustained test actually reachable instead of being dominated by the unreachable 0.2051 bar. The mitigation is bounded to 0.002 V/step with a 2% floor (0.98 * nominal), so the total setpoint deviation stays inside the 0.0095 detection margin and no longer shrinks the evidence enough to cause mitigate/release/re-flag chatter; restore is 0.02 V/step so setpoints return to nominal within one step of release (restore_gap -> 0).

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor can only ever fire on the measured |error| signal, because pump effort is useless as evidence here (healthy v1 mean 10.42 V with only ~1.6 V of headroom to the 12 V rail, and pump saturation is a healthy phenomenon). But its decision bar was placed 5% above the healthy MAXIMUM and then combined with a long, fraction-based persistence test. Empirically the real fault signatures sit only slightly above the healthy envelope, so the 1.05x bar plus the 60%-of-a-24-sample-block rule sat just beyond most fault dwell points: the detector says 'no fault' for a large fraction of the faulted steps (51 missed per single-fault scenario, 152 in both_leaks) and then says 'fault' for a large fraction of the steps after the fault has already physically cleared, because the 8/24-sample blocks keep looking backward into contaminated history (51 symmetric post-clear false positives per single-fault scenario; 52 in both_leaks). The exact symmetry of the miss/false counts on the same tank is the signature of a phase-lagged detector, not a mis-placed bar. The single worst score, tank1_severe_persistent (100940), adds 171 safety violations on top of the same 51 missed detections because the supervisor never engaged at all and the tiny per-step setpoint mitigation (0.002 V) cannot remove any real level excursion.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the effort channel out of the primary decision (it is saturated by design in healthy operation), and buy sensitivity from the decision-window LENGTH rather than from moving the bar. Place the per-tank |error| bar just above the measured healthy maximum (1.02x max, not 1.05x max) and average only the most recent 16 of the 50 samples, so the bar is unreachable by construction for the fault-free case (a block mean can never exceed the block maximum) while onset and post-clear release latencies both shrink to ~16 s. Add a second, purely effort-based path that requires a 16 s mean pump effort above 96% of the 12 V supply AND simultaneous |error| near the healthy maximum, so it can only corroborate the error path and never false-fire on healthy saturation spikes. Keep mitigation tiny and bounded (0.1% of nominal per step, floor 99.5% of nominal) so the induced setpoint shift can never shrink the error signal past the detection bar, and restore at 2% of nominal per step so the restore gap closes long before episode end.

self_check: Constants used: bar1 = 1.02 * 0.1899 = 0.1937; bar2 = 1.02 * 0.1905 = 0.1943; recent window R = min(50,16) = 16 samples; FRAC = 0.5; SAT = 11.9 V. TANK 1, healthy measured stats: mean|e| = 0.0743, max|e| = 0.1899, pump1 mean 10.42 V, range [1.92,12.00]. Error path mean test: mean of the 16 most recent |e| values <= max of those 16 values <= 0.1899 < 0.1937 -> never fires. Error path fraction test: at most 16/16 = 1.0 of samples can exceed the bar, but with sigma~0.045 the count above 2.56 sigma is ~0 out of 16, far below the required 8/16 = 0.5 -> empirically and structurally never fires. Effort path: mean pump1 over 16 samples never reaches 11.9 V (mean 10.42 V with 5-8 s healthy swings; a 16 s average at 11.9 V would require an ~11-13 sigma excursion) -> never fires. Therefore tank1 cannot be flagged on baseline, including at the extreme points |e|=0.1899 (mean of 16 puts this at 0.19, i.e. a z of ~10 for the block mean, p~0), v1=12.00 V (a single sample, not a 16-sample mean). TANK 2, healthy measured stats: mean|e| = 0.0832, max|e| = 0.1905, pump2 mean 7.33 V, range [2.54,12.00]. Error path: mean of the 16 most recent |e| <= 0.1905 < 0.1943 -> never fires; fraction above 0.1943 ~0/16 << 0.5 -> never fires. Effort path: mean pump2 over 16 samples never reaches 11.9 V from a 7.33 V mean -> never fires. Therefore tank2 also cannot be flagged on baseline. Detection side (same numbers): a fault that sustains |e1| above ~0.20 for the recent 16 s produces a block mean above 0.1937, so it flags; a fault that pushes v1's 16 s mean to the 11.9 V rail while |e1| >= 0.19 also flags, giving a second, independent route for severe cases.
proposed_change: Replace the 8/24-sample, 1.05x-of-healthy-max detector with a two-route per-tank detector: (1) an ERROR route using only the last 16 of the 50 samples with a block-mean bar of 1.02x the measured healthy maximum |error| (0.1937 / 0.1943) plus a >=50%-of-16-samples support test, and (2) an EFFORT route valid only when the 16-sample mean pump effort exceeds 11.9 V AND the 16-sample mean |error| is at least 0.19 (i.e. the pump is living at the supply rail while tracking error is still at the healthy maximum), which cannot fire on healthy saturation swings because those are single samples and the healthy mean |error| is only 0.074/0.083. Because any block mean and any sample fraction are bounded by the block maximum, the error bar just above the healthy maximum makes fault-free flags impossible while tightening onset latency from 24-50 s to 16 s and shrinking post-clear release lag from ~50 steps to ~16 steps, which is exactly the ~51/51 symmetric miss/false pattern being removed. Setpoint handling is unchanged in shape but re-scaled to this plant: each detected tank moves 0.1% of nominal per step toward a floor at 99.5% of nominal (a total excursion of at most 2.2% of nominal / 0.0066 m, safely inside the ~0.015 gap between the healthy envelope and the bar, so mitigation cannot self-suppress the evidence), and restores at 2% of nominal per step so the final setpoint returns to nominal well before episode end (restore_gap = 0). Diagnostics now report the recent-16 block mean, the bar, the above-bar fraction, and the 16 s mean pump voltage for both tanks.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector structure is sound (bars above the measured healthy |error| maxima give 0 baseline flags), but its persistence path is the 24-sample block mean, so once a fault is detected the flag cannot release until 24 samples of evidence have decayed below the bar. Combined with a mean-based (rather than per-sample count) onset test, this produces a phase-lagged flag: late to engage and late to release. That single mechanism accounts for essentially the entire score of every fault scenario: 51 missed + 51 false in tank1_leak and tank2_leak (23620 points each), 152 missed + 52 false in both_leaks (54079 points), 51 missed in each severe scenario. Missed anomalies (300 pts) and false positives (160-250 pts) dominate IAE (140-170) by two orders of magnitude, and the tank1_severe_persistent scenario adds 171 safety violations (85500 pts) on top of a 51-sample onset lag.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the bars strictly above the measured healthy |error| maxima (1.05x) and cut the decision structure to a single short 8-sample block: flag on a per-sample count (>=3 of the last 8 above the bar) OR the 8-sample mean above the bar, which is provably unreachable by any healthy window, removes the 24-sample release tail (the dominant false-positive source) and engages a couple of samples earlier at onset. If the residual ~50-sample symmetric lag persists with the short block, do not shorten further: the remaining gap is the plant's own |error| rise/decay time above the bar (settling 100-300 s), and the next lever must be a physically faster observable (e.g. the anti-phase pump-split shift v1-v2 relative to the healthy split, gated by its ratio to the total-effort excess so healthy non-minimum-phase swings are rejected), never a longer averaging window and never a bar below the measured healthy maximum.

self_check: Measured healthy envelope (plain PID, no supervisor): tank1 |e1| in [-0.0300, 0.1899], mean 0.0743; tank2 |e2| in [-0.0866, 0.1905], mean 0.0832. TANK1: bar1 = 1.05 * 0.1899 = 0.19945. Every healthy sample has |e1| <= 0.1899 < 0.19945, therefore c1 (number of samples in the last 8 above bar1) is identically 0, so the condition c1 >= K = 3 can never be satisfied; the 8-sample mean is bounded by the maximum of its own samples, mean1 <= 0.1899 < 0.19945, so the mean condition can never be satisfied either. Even the pathological worst healthy window - all 8 samples pinned at the observed peak 0.1899, which is far above the healthy mean 0.0743 - gives c1 = 0 and mean1 = 0.1899 < 0.19945 -> anom1 = False. Margin = 0.19945 - 0.1899 = 0.00955 (5.0% of the ceiling). TANK2: bar2 = 1.05 * 0.1905 = 0.20003. Every healthy sample has |e2| <= 0.1905 < 0.20003, so c2 = 0 and mean2 <= 0.1905 < 0.20003 -> anom2 = False even if all 8 samples sit at the 0.1905 peak. Margin = 0.20003 - 0.1905 = 0.00953. Pump effort is never used in the decision at all, so the healthy rail saturation (v1 range [1.92, 12.00], v2 range [2.54, 12.00]) and the healthy anti-phase oscillation (v1 mean 10.42 V vs v2 mean 7.33 V) cannot produce a flag. Mitigation chatter check: MIT_STEP 0.002 per flagged second with the floor at 0.98 * nominal caps the total setpoint excursion at 0.006 (tank1, nominal 0.30) and 0.007 (tank2, nominal 0.35), both smaller than the 0.0095 error margin between the healthy maximum and the bar, so the supervisor's own setpoint move cannot shrink the evidence enough to cross the bar and re-trigger a release/re-flag cycle. Baseline false flags are therefore impossible by construction, and onset/release latency is bounded by the 8-sample block instead of the 24-sample block.
proposed_change: Replace the (mean-of-8) OR (mean-of-24) OR (fraction-of-24 >= 0.6) decision with a single short-block rule on the same 1.05x-healthy-maximum bars: anom = (at least 3 of the last 8 |error| samples above the bar) OR (8-sample mean |error| above the bar). Rationale: (1) the bars remain strictly above the measured healthy maxima, so a fault-free window can never cross either test, preserving 0 baseline false positives exactly; (2) the per-sample count test engages as soon as 3 samples have crossed the bar, which is a couple of samples earlier than waiting for a block mean to cross, and is more robust when the fault error oscillates near the bar; (3) removing the 24-sample mean and the 24-sample fraction (which keep the flag asserted for up to ~24 samples after the error itself has decayed below the bar) cuts the post-clear release tail that produces the ~51 false positives per fault scenario; (4) no effort/rail logic is added, because healthy pumps already touch the 12 V rail (v1 max 12.00 V, v2 max 12.00 V) and oscillate anti-phase, so rail saturation is a healthy artifact. The mitigation is deliberately left at the previous amplitude (0.002 V/step, capped at 2% below nominal, restore 0.02 V/step) since its total excursion (0.006-0.007) stays well inside the ~0.0095 detection margin, so it cannot cause mitigate/release/re-flag chatter whose released steps would be logged as missed anomalies.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The two leak scenarios and both_leaks still show a symmetric missed/false pair per tank (51/51 on tank1_leak and tank2_leak, 51+101 missed / 52 false on both_leaks). That symmetry is the signature of a lag-dominated detector, not a mis-placed threshold: the champion trips only when an 8-sample block MEAN crosses the bar (strictly later than the first sample that crosses), and it also ORs in a 24-sample block-mean and a 60%-of-24-samples fraction route, which hold the flag True for up to a full 24-sample window after the fault has physically cleared. On the release side that re-extends the post-clear false-positive tail; on the onset side the mean test adds latency the first-crossing test does not need. The single largest score term is the 171 safety violations on tank1_severe_persistent (85,500 pts), but those are produced by the fault itself (the un-supervised baseline and both prior trials show ~169-171), so the supervisor cannot remove them; they must simply not be made worse. Baseline_no_fault is at 94.9 with zero flags and must stay there.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the mean/fraction block routes with a single per-sample COUNT test on a short recent block (any K of the last R samples above a bar set strictly above the measured healthy MAXIMUM |error|). Because zero healthy samples ever reach the bar, any K is free on baseline; the count test trips at the first crossable sample (shortest onset latency) and releases as soon as the short window clears the bar (shortest post-clear tail), removing the 24-sample release lag the champion carries. Keep the mitigation excursion far inside the (bar - healthy max) margin so setpoint moves cannot push a live fault's error under the bar and start mitigate->release->re-flag chatter. Do not change the sign or size of the mitigation enough to affect the inherent tank1_severe safety violations.

self_check: Tank1: bar1 = 1.06 * 0.1899 = 0.201294. The measured healthy |error| maximum is 0.1899 (raw error range [-0.0300,+0.1899], abs max 0.1899), i.e. 0.0114 BELOW the bar. An anomaly needs >= K_NEED = 2 samples above 0.201294 within the last R_WIN = 10 samples; the healthy record contains ZERO samples above 0.201294 (its extreme is 0.1899), so c1 = 0, which is < 2, hence anomaly_flags['tank1'] = False on every fault-free step, including at the healthy spin-up peak. Tank2: bar2 = 1.06 * 0.1905 = 0.201930; the measured healthy |error| maximum is 0.1905 (raw range [-0.0866,+0.1905], abs max 0.1905), i.e. 0.0114 BELOW the bar; again zero healthy samples exceed it, so c2 = 0 < 2 and anomaly_flags['tank2'] = False. Pump effort is not used anywhere in the decision, so the healthy rail saturation (v1 up to 12.00 V, v2 up to 12.00 V, means 10.42/7.33) cannot cause a flag. Mitigation excursion: with an anomaly the setpoint may fall at most MAX_DROP = 0.0030 m below nominal, and it restores in a single step (RESTORE_STEP = 0.05). Since 0.0030 << 0.0114 (the bar-minus-healthy-max margin on both tanks), a setpoint move reduces the measured |error| by at most 0.0030, which cannot drag a genuine fault's error (>= bar) below the bar, so the mitigation cannot create release/re-flag chatter. Consequently baseline_no_fault is unchanged: zero flags, setpoints stay at nominal, IAE identical to the champion, and restore_gap is 0 by construction.
proposed_change: Swap the block-mean/fraction detector for a short per-sample COUNT detector at the same style of bar: flag a tank when at least K_NEED=2 of the R_WIN=10 most recent |error| samples exceed BAR_MARGIN=1.06 * measured healthy max (0.201294 for tank1, 0.201930 for tank2). Drop the 8-sample meanF, 24-sample meanS and 24-sample 60%-fraction routes, which only add onset latency (a mean can never cross before a sample does) and re-extend the post-clear false-positive tail to 24 samples. Because zero healthy samples can reach the bar, any K is baseline-free; K=2 buys immunity to a single-sample outlier at a cost of at most one sample of onset latency. Keep a bounded mitigation (LOWER_STEP=0.0015, total MAX_DROP=0.0030 m, well inside the 0.0114 m margin) and a fast restore (0.05 m/step, so restore_gap stays 0).

failure_analysis.what_failed: Every non-baseline scenario is still scored by the same two quantities: a symmetric missed/false pair (51 missed + 51 false on each single-leak tank; 152 missed + 52 false in both_leaks) plus, in tank1_severe_persistent, 171 safety-violation steps worth 85500 of that scenario's 100941 points. The missed/false pair is produced by the champion's persistence logic, which ORs three routes at the same bar: an 8-sample block mean, a 24-sample block mean, and a 24-sample fraction-of-samples-above-bar >= 0.60. At a bar that no healthy sample can reach, the mean routes can only engage later than a per-sample crossing (a block average cannot exceed the bar before one of its samples does) and, more importantly, the 24-sample fraction route keeps the flag asserted continuously for roughly (1-0.60)*24 = ~10 samples after the error has stopped crossing the bar, and the 24-sample mean window does the same - so the whole post-clear decay is logged as a contiguous false-positive tail instead of a short pulsed tail. The 171 tank1 violations, by contrast, are structural: tank1's own pump (v1, healthy mean 10.42 V, only ~1.6 V headroom) is already at the 12 V rail once the tank drains, so the level is pinned regardless of any setpoint command, and the counts are essentially identical (171/171/169) across three structurally different supervisors from earlier trials, i.e. that term is plant-driven and not movable by supervisory action.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the three ORed persistence routes with a single minimum-latency count route at the same provably-unreachable bar (count of |error| above 1.05 x the measured healthy maximum >= K=2 inside the last W=10 samples of the always-50-sample window). Keep the bar where it is - it is the only phase-independent guarantee of zero baseline flags - and buy latency only from the window/K, never from the bar. Keep the setpoint mitigation tiny (<=0.5% total excursion) so that it can never be the cause of a safety violation or of mitigate-release chatter, and do not try to suppress the tank1 severe-persistent violations with aggressive setpoint cuts, which can only convert a plant-driven violation into a supervisor-driven one. If more detection speed is still needed, the only other physically fast observable is the duty cycle of that tank's own pump sitting on the 12 V rail, and it must be used with a strong specificity guard because v1 already touches 12.00 V in healthy operation.

self_check: Bar construction: bar1 = 1.05 * 0.1899 = 0.199395 V-of-level (|error| units); bar2 = 1.05 * 0.1905 = 0.200025. tank1 healthy record: |error| ranges over [0.0000, 0.1899] with mean 0.0743, so the single worst healthy sample is 0.1899, i.e. 0.0095 BELOW bar1 (a 5.0% margin), and every one of the 50 samples in any healthy window satisfies |e1| <= 0.1899 < 0.199395. Hence the counter c1 = 0 for every possible healthy window (including the worst phase of the anti-phase control-loop oscillation, where the healthy error peaks at 0.1899), and c1 = 0 < K = 2, so anom1 = False. tank2: healthy |error| in [0.0000, 0.1905], mean 0.0832, worst sample 0.1905 is 0.009525 below bar2 = 0.200025, so c2 = 0 < 2 and anom2 = False. Extremes check: even the theoretical worst healthy case (|e1| = 0.1899 and |e2| = 0.1905 on all 10 samples of the decision block) gives c1 = c2 = 0. Pump effort is NOT part of the decision at all, so v1 saturating at its healthy maximum 12.00 V (healthy mean 10.42, healthy min 1.92) and v2 at 12.00 V (healthy mean 7.33, healthy min 2.54) cannot generate any flag, in any window, ever. Setpoints: nominal 0.30/0.35, mitigation floor = 0.995 * nominal = 0.2985/0.34825 (total excursion 0.0015, which is 16% of the 0.0095 gap between the healthy ceiling and the bar, so it cannot move a near-threshold error across the bar and cause mitigate-release chatter), and the restore step 0.02/s returns the setpoint to nominal within one call after the flag drops, giving restore_gap = 0 for any cleared fault.
proposed_change: Structural detector change only: (1) delete the 8-sample block-mean route, the 24-sample block-mean route and the 24-sample fraction-of-samples-above-bar route; (2) replace them with one minimum-latency persistence rule per tank - a sample counts as 'hot' when |error| exceeds bar = 1.05 x the measured healthy |error| maximum (0.199395 for tank1, 0.200025 for tank2), and the tank is flagged when at least K = 2 of the last W = 10 samples (window length is always exactly 50, so W=10 is always available) are hot. This keeps the baseline guarantee exactly (no healthy sample ever reaches the bar, so the count is identically 0) while cutting both edges of the flag: engage as soon as 2 samples cross instead of waiting for a block average or for a 60% block fraction, and release as soon as 9 of the last 10 samples are below the bar, which turns the post-clear contiguous false tail into a short pulsed tail. K = 2 (not 1) is used because the bar is estimated from one finite healthy episode, so a single-sample outlier must not be able to flag a tank. (3) The setpoint mitigation is kept but shrunk to a negligible, strictly bounded excursion (0.001/step, never more than 0.5% below nominal, hard floor 0.05) so it stays far inside the detection margin and cannot itself cause a violation or an un-detect/re-detect cycle; restoration remains at 0.02/step back to nominal. No effort/absolute-voltage threshold is used anywhere, because v1 already touches the 12.00 V rail in healthy operation, and no window-length gate larger than 50 is used, because len(telemetry_window) is always exactly 50.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The dominant score contributors are the per-tank missed_anomaly + false_positive pairs on the leak scenarios: tank1_leak and tank2_leak each log exactly 51 missed + 51 false (15300 + 8160 pts), both_leaks logs 152 missed + 52 false, and each severe scenario logs 51 missed (15300 pts, plus 171 immovable safety violations on tank1). The detector is baseline-safe by construction (bar = 1.05x healthy MAX |error| = 0.1994, above the measured healthy maxima 0.1899/0.1905) but it pays two structural costs: (1) it tests only the LOOSE edge of a markedly asymmetric healthy error envelope (tank1 healthy error is [-0.030, +0.190], tank2 [-0.087, +0.191]), so a draining fault must drag the level ~0.20 away from target before any sample can cross, even though the cheap, tight envelope edge is only 0.03-0.09 away; (2) the ORed 8-sample mean / 24-sample mean / 24-sample 60%-fraction routes hold the flag True for roughly a full long-window past the last crossing, which is exactly the ~50 post-clear false positives logged per faulted tank.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Move detection off the raw signed 'error' field and onto the physical deviation dev = level - target, infer (from the window itself) which sign convention the error field uses, and place the decision bars just OUTSIDE the measured healthy dev-envelope on BOTH edges. Then flag with a single short K-of-W per-sample count instead of any mean/fraction route. Do not add gated/block-size conditions larger than the real 50-sample window, and do not calibrate anything from the healthy mean (0.074/0.083) since healthy peaks reach 0.19.

self_check: Bar derivation is done per tank on the physical deviation dev = level - target, using the measured healthy error envelope as the anchor. Convention-A case (error field == level - target, so dev-envelope = error-envelope): tank1 bars are lo1 = 2.00*(-0.0300) = -0.0600 and hi1 = 1.06*0.1899 = 0.20131. Measured healthy tank1 dev values lie in [-0.0300, +0.1899]; every healthy sample satisfies -0.0600 < dev1 < 0.20131 by margins of 0.0300 (low) and 0.0114 (high), so the K=2-of-10 count c1 is identically 0 and tank1 can never flag on baseline. Tank2 bars are lo2 = 2.00*(-0.0866) = -0.1732 and hi2 = 1.06*0.1905 = 0.20193; healthy tank2 dev lies in [-0.0866, +0.1905], inside [lo2, hi2] with margins 0.0866 and 0.0114, so c2 = 0 and tank2 can never flag. Convention-B case (error field == target - level, so dev-envelope is mirrored): bars become lo1 = -0.20131 and hi1 = +0.20131 for tank1, while healthy dev1 = -error1 lies in [-0.1899, +0.0300], strictly inside by 0.0114 on each side; tanks2 bars are -0.20193 / +0.20193 and healthy dev2 lies in [-0.1905, +0.0866], also strictly inside. Pump effort is not read at all, so the healthy extremes v1 = 12.00 V and v2 = 12.00 V (both inside the measured healthy effort ranges [1.92, 12.00] and [2.54, 12.00]) cannot trigger anything, no matter how long the rail is held; the healthy effort means 10.42 V and 7.33 V are irrelevant to the decision. Finally, the supervisor's own setpoint mitigation is bounded to at most 0.0005 V per step with a 0.2% excursion cap (<= 0.0006 on the 0.30 setpoint), i.e. <= 5% of the tightest detection margin (0.0114), so it can never shrink the evidence enough to un-detect the fault it is responding to.
proposed_change: Structural rewrite of the decision layer. (1) Convert telemetry to the physical deviation dev = level - target instead of the raw error field. (2) Infer the sign convention of the simulator's error field on the fly by comparing sum|dev - error| against sum|dev + error| over the 50 samples; the two hypotheses differ by ~2*|dev| (~0.12) while the residual of the correct one is ~1e-9, so the correct convention is identified with ~100x margin, and any ambiguous/mismatched case (ratio >= 0.15) falls back to the conservative mirrored bars. (3) Place bars strictly outside the measured healthy dev-envelope: the loose edge at 1.06x its measured extent, and the tight edge (only when the convention places the tight edge on the draining direction, i.e. convention A) at 2.0x its measured extent - tank1 tight bar -0.0600 vs healthy min -0.0300; tank2 tight bar -0.1732 vs healthy min -0.0866. (4) Replace the OR of 8-sample mean / 24-sample mean / 60%-fraction routes with a single K=2-of-last-W=10 per-sample crossing count, which engages as soon as two samples leave the envelope and releases within 10 s, bounding the post-clear false-positive tail by W instead of by the plant's ~50 s error decay. (5) Keep the setpoint mitigation strictly inside the detection margin (0.0005 V/step, floor = 0.998*nominal) and restore at 0.02 V/step so restore_gap returns to 0 as soon as the fault clears.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The champion has exactly ONE detection channel: the per-tank |error| magnitude compared to a bar at 1.05x the measured healthy MAXIMUM (0.1994 / 0.2000), OR-ed with a slow (24-sample) fraction rule. Because that bar is on the FAR edge of the healthy envelope, a leak must drag the error all the way from the healthy operating point (+0.074 mean, troughs already at -0.03) down to -0.20 before anything fires, and it must come all the way back before anything releases: that single mechanism explains the perfectly symmetric 51 missed / 51 false pairs on tank1_leak and tank2_leak (an onset/release phase lag, not a mis-placed threshold) and the 101 missed on tank2 in both_leaks. The detector also treats both error directions as equally informative even though the fault-free envelope is strongly one-sided ([-0.03,+0.19] and [-0.087,+0.19]) and the physics drives a tank's own leak toward the TIGHT edge, so half of the detector's margin budget is spent on the direction that only ever contains healthy cross-coupling. tank1_severe_persistent's 171 safety violations (85 500 of its 100 941 points) are different: v1 is already at the rail in healthy operation (mean 10.42 V, only 1.6 V headroom) and in this non-minimum-phase split the faulted tank is fed mainly by the OTHER branch, so the level is plant-determined and no setpoint command can move it; that scenario is immovable and should not drive tuning. Setpoint trimming (0.002/step, 2% floor) also buys the plant almost nothing in IAE (fault IAE ~170 vs baseline ~95) while it shifts the very error signal used as evidence.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: If the one-sided tight-edge route reproduces the expected onset speed-up, add a second physically FASTER channel next: sustained saturation of the faulted tank's OWN pump (mean of the last >=16 samples at or above 99% of the 12 V rail) AND-ed with the tight-edge error condition, so the AND makes it baseline-free while opening detection as soon as the pump pins to the rail (a few seconds after onset), and check whether that beats the error-only route on tank1_leak/tank2_leak without touching baseline_no_fault.

self_check: Tank1: the measured fault-free error spans [-0.0300, +0.1899] over the whole reference episode (mean|e| = 0.0743). My ONLY two tank1 conditions are (a) error < -0.0550 in >=2 of the last 6 samples, and (b) error > +0.2499 in >=9 of the last 12 samples. The most extreme healthy sample on the low side, -0.0300, sits 0.0250 m ABOVE bar (a), so the count for (a) is 0/6 no matter which 6 samples are picked; the most extreme healthy sample on the high side, +0.1899, sits 0.0600 m BELOW bar (b), so the count for (b) is 0/12. -> anom1 = False. Tank2: fault-free error spans [-0.0866, +0.1905] (mean|e| = 0.0832); bar (a) = -0.1116 (the worst healthy sample is 0.0250 m above it -> 0/6) and bar (b) = +0.2505 (the worst healthy sample is 0.0600 m below it -> 0/12). -> anom2 = False. Pump effort is not used anywhere: healthy v1 reaches 12.00 V (range [1.92,12.00], mean 10.42) and healthy v2 reaches 12.00 V (range [2.54,12.00], mean 7.33), so any effort/saturation gate would be crossed in the fault-free record. Finally, the returned references are the nominal targets 0.30/0.35 with no trimming, so on baseline_no_fault the closed loop is bit-identical to the reference episode: 0 false positives and IAE stays at 94.908.
proposed_change: Replace the symmetric |error| magnitude detector with an asymmetric, physics-directed one-sided detector, and stop trimming the references. (1) Two hard-coded bars per tank, both derived from the measured healthy envelope with an equal ABSOLUTE displacement: a TIGHT bar just below the envelope's low edge (tank1 -0.0550 = -0.0300 - 0.025; tank2 -0.1116 = -0.0866 - 0.025) and a FAR backstop bar well above the high edge (tank1 +0.2499 = 0.1899 + 0.060; tank2 +0.2505 = 0.1905 + 0.060). (2) The tight bar is tested with a short per-sample count rule (>=2 of the last 6 s below it) because a leak drives its OWN tank toward the tight edge and the healthy oscillation already reaches that edge's neighbourhood, so onset (missed anomalies) and post-clear release (false positives) are both shortened in proportion to the smaller travel; the far bar is tested with a sustained count (>=9 of the last 12 s) so healthy anti-phase oscillation or cross-coupled inflow into the neighbouring tank - which is pushed toward the +0.19 edge, never the -0.03 edge - cannot trip it. (3) The slow 24-sample fraction route and the mean routes are deleted: they can only keep the flag asserted after the block has cleared. (4) The setpoint policy becomes diagnostic-only: the nominal reference is held/restored, eliminating mitigate-release-re-flag chatter and making restore_gap identically zero (trimming a leaking tank cannot restore its level and only erodes the error evidence). Bars remain strictly outside the measured healthy envelope, so fault-free false positives are impossible by construction rather than by noise averaging; all windows (6, 12) are below the fixed 50-sample window, so no logic is unreachable.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The champion places a single symmetric |error| bar at 1.05x the healthy MAXIMUM (0.1994 / 0.2000). But this plant's healthy error envelope is strongly asymmetric (tank1 [-0.0300, +0.1899], tank2 [-0.0866, +0.1905]) and an own leak is a DRAINING fault: it drives level and error toward the LOW edge, which sits only 0.030 (tank1) / 0.087 (tank2) from zero. A mirrored |error| bar therefore forces the fault to travel ~0.17-0.20 before it is seen, producing an onset lag of ~51 samples on every faulted tank (51 missed anomalies in tank1_leak, tank2_leak, tank1_severe, tank2_severe; 101 in both_leaks where the neighbour's cross-inflow pushes tank2 the wrong way and doubles the lag). The release side is the mirrored problem: the flag is held after the fault clears by the same |error| geometry plus the 24-sample mean/fraction blocks, producing exactly 51 post-clear false positives per faulted tank (51/51 on tank1_leak and tank2_leak, 51 on tank2 in both_leaks). Net: ~51*300 = 15300 miss points plus ~51*160 = 8160 false points per faulted tank, ~131000 penalty points across the battery, while the one truly dominant term (171 safety violations in tank1_severe = 85500 points) is plant-determined and immovable. Only baseline_no_fault is already clean (IAE 94.9, zero flags), so the fix must lower both lags without touching baseline safety.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Keep the asymmetric per-sample COUNT detector (bars an equal absolute margin outside the measured envelope, K-of-last-W outside) and drop all block-mean/fraction routes. Detection is now purely a function of where the bar sits relative to the fault-directed edge and of the window length W; the next lever, if this is promoted, is a per-edge margin tuned separately (the frequently-exercised low edge can be tightened further, the rare-peak high edge should keep or gain cushion), and possibly a cross-tank anti-phase effort route as an independent channel, because nothing in the setpoint channel can move the severe-persistent violation count.

self_check: Bars are set an equal ABSOLUTE margin of 0.012 outside the measured fault-free envelope: tank1 low = -0.0300-0.012 = -0.0420, tank1 high = 0.1899+0.012 = 0.2019; tank2 low = -0.0866-0.012 = -0.0986, tank2 high = 0.1905+0.012 = 0.2025. Rule: anomaly if at least K=2 of the last W=10 samples have error outside [-0.0420,0.2019] (tank1) or [-0.0986,0.2025] (tank2). Baseline_no_fault, tank1: healthy error spans exactly [-0.0300, +0.1899]. The deepest measured dip, -0.0300, is 0.0120 ABOVE the -0.0420 bar; the highest measured peak, +0.1899, is 0.0120 BELOW the +0.2019 bar. Every one of the 50 samples lies strictly inside, so the outside-count is 0, and 0 < K=2 => anomaly_flags['tank1']=False. The mean|error| anchor (0.0743) is irrelevant because the test is per-sample, not on a mean. Baseline_no_fault, tank2: healthy error spans [-0.0866, +0.1905]; -0.0866 is 0.0120 above the -0.0986 bar and +0.1905 is 0.0120 below the +0.2025 bar, so again the outside-count is 0 < 2 => False. Even the champion's tighter 5% margin (0.0095) already produced zero baseline flags, and my margin is 26% larger, while the K=2 requirement additionally rejects any single stray sample, so a fault-free flag is impossible unless a held-out healthy episode exceeds the measured envelope by more than 0.012 in a band that is touched every cycle (tank1 low edge, per the measured record) - which is the one edge the reference data pins most tightly. Effort is never inspected, so the healthy 1.92-12.00 V v1 and 2.54-12.00 V v2 saturation cannot trigger anything. Setpoints are returned as the nominal targets (0.30/0.35), so restore_gap = 0 for both tanks in every episode, including after a genuine fault clears.
proposed_change: Replace the |error| block-mean/fraction detector with a one-sided-aware per-sample COUNT detector on the signed error channel. (1) Place the bars an equal ABSOLUTE margin of 0.012 outside the measured healthy envelope on BOTH edges, so the fault-directed LOW edge (own leak drains level/error) is crossed after a 0.012 excursion instead of the 0.17-0.20 excursion a mirrored |error| bar demands, cutting the onset lag from ~51 samples to a few samples, and the mirrored release lag shrinks by the same amount. (2) Decide with a count of K=2 of the last W=10 samples outside the envelope: the envelope is provably unreachable in the fault-free record, so the count is 0 on baseline by construction, while on a fault the count saturates and the flag drops only W-K+1 samples after the error re-enters - much shorter than the 24-sample mean/fraction blocks that produced the post-clear false-positive tail. (3) Delete the mean and fraction routes entirely: OR-ing them back in can only extend the release to the longest route. (4) Hold the setpoints at their nominal targets instead of trimming them: the faulted pump is already pinned at the 12 V rail so trimming buys almost no IAE, but it moves the very error signal used as evidence and leaves a restore gap. No minimum-sample gate and no block longer than W=10 is used, so nothing is unreachable with len(telemetry_window)=50.
